blocks.text: That distinction is worth keeping in mind as governments prepare for the UN biodiversity conference in Yerevan, Armenia, from October 19 to 30. COP17 will hold the first global review of collective progress in implementing the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, adopted in 2022.

blocks.text: The framework's targets run to 2030. This review gives governments an opportunity to examine how their commitments are turning into action while there is still time to change course.

blocks.text: Target 2 calls for at least 30% of degraded ecosystems to be under effective restoration by 2030. That wording is important: “under restoration” is different from claiming that every ecosystem will be fully recovered by then.

inline.text: Target 2

calls for at least 30% of degraded ecosystems to be under effective restoration by 2030. That wording is important: “under restoration” is different from claiming that every ecosystem will be fully recovered by then.

blocks.text: The Secretariat's guidance recognizes that restoration is a long-term process. Effective activities need resources and monitoring over time. The ability to restore a place later also should not become a justification for degrading it now.

inline.text: The Secretariat's guidance recognizes that restoration is a long-term process. Effective activities need resources and monitoring over time. The ability to restore a place later also should not become a justification for degrading it now.

blocks.text: For a hypothetical wetland project, an initial intervention might reopen water connections or remove a barrier. The evaluation would need to follow whether the intended conditions develop and persist. Which measures are useful depends on the project's goals: water levels, vegetation, habitat use, or another defined response.

blocks.text: The framework also makes finance part of implementation. Target 19 seeks at least $200 billion annually from all sources by 2030. Within that broader goal, it includes international financial flows to developing countries of at least $20 billion per year by 2025 and $30 billion by 2030.

Target 19

seeks at least $200 billion annually from all sources by 2030. Within that broader goal, it includes international financial flows to developing countries of at least $20 billion per year by 2025 and $30 billion by 2030.

blocks.text: These are target amounts, not evidence that the money has arrived. The $30 billion international component also should not be added to the $200 billion as if it were a separate total.
